key_insight: Plasma p-tau217 was elevated in both Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), while the p-tau217/NfL ratio distinguished ALS from AD better than p-tau217 alone.
clinical_relevance: These findings suggest that interpreting p-tau217 alongside NfL may improve research-level differentiation of ALS and AD, but do not establish a clinical diagnostic test.
method: Studied 551 participants across 10 diagnostic groups, including 45 amyloid-PET-negative cognitively unimpaired controls.
Measured baseline plasma p-tau217, p-tau181, Aβ42/40, NfL, and GFAP.
Compared biomarker profiles and ROC-AUC performance; tested clinical and longitudinal associations within ALS.
evidence_signal: The p-tau217/NfL ratio distinguished ALS from AD with an ROC-AUC of 0.92 (95% CI 0.85–0.97), versus 0.65 (95% CI 0.52–0.76) for p-tau217 alone.
watch_item: Amyloid positivity was inferred from p-tau217 rather than independently confirmed across patient groups, limiting interpretation of elevated p-tau217.
paper_title: Plasma phosphorylated tau species across neurodegenerative and cerebrovascular diseases: An ONDRI study
